cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, and he skips the small talk with the LORD: "I call upon You, O LORD; come quickly to me. Hear my voice when I call to You." Not "whenever You get a minute, Lord." QUICKLY!

cards.question: David asks for his prayer to be set before the LORD like something from Israel's worship. What is it?

cards.text: And his uplifted hands? David wants them to be like the evening offering. I lift my hands like that too, friend, but usually it's because the timer went off and I can't find the oven mitts.

Then David turns the spotlight on himself: "Set a guard, O LORD, over my mouth; keep watch at the door of my lips." A GUARD? I need a whole security team. Half the stuff I've said in this bakery should've been stopped at the door!

cards.question: David asks the LORD to keep watch at the door of his lips. What does he want help with?

cards.text: Then David goes deeper than his mouth. He asks, "Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing."

cards.question: David asks not to take part in works of wickedness with men who do ___.
True or false: David asks to enjoy the delicacies of men who do iniquity, as long as he stays out of their works.

cards.text: No fancy delicacies from that crowd. Then David says something you don't hear every day: he's fine getting hit, as long as it's from the right person.

cards.question: Who is David willing to let strike him?
How does David see a rebuke from a righteous man?

answers.text: as an act of loving devotion
as a punishment he has earned
as a test of his pride

cards.text: He even calls it oil for his head and says, "let me not refuse it." Me? A baker tells me my oven's running hot and I get defensive for three whole seconds. Then I check. ...It's running hot.

cards.question: True or false: David says his prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked.

cards.text: David's still praying to the LORD. Now he looks ahead to a time "When their rulers are thrown down from the cliffs."

cards.question: When those rulers are thrown down from the cliffs, what does David say the people will do?
True or false: David says the people will listen to his words because they are afraid of him.

cards.text: Then the psalm gets heavy. David says, "so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol."

cards.question: David compares those bones scattered at the mouth of Sheol to a picture from everyday life. What is it?

cards.text: And then David says one little word: "But." Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer waiting for a "but." That's a GOOD word.

cards.question: Even with bones scattered at the mouth of Sheol, David says his eyes are fixed on ___.
True or false: David says he seeks refuge in his own strength.

cards.text: Then David asks God to keep him from the snares and lures the evildoers have laid for him. Snares AND lures? These folks didn't set one trap. They built a whole obstacle course!

cards.question: David asks for the wicked to fall into their own ___ while he passes by in ___.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says "I lift my hands like that too" and jokes about not finding the oven mitts. He has no hands. He uses his mustache as hands, so this contradicts who he is, and the joke doesn't click for a baker who knows him.

rule.text: A cookie stamper with a huge French mustache that he uses as hands. He holds, points, waves and packs cookie boxes with it.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card gives away the answer to card 5 before the baker picks. It quotes "Set a guard, O LORD, over my mouth" and jokes that "Half the stuff I've said...should've been stopped at the door." Card 5 then asks what David wants help with, and the answer is "guarding what he says."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "justice" and "mercy" make the line nonsense ("works of wickedness with men who do mercy"), so they aren't believable. "iniquity" is also the only Bible-sounding word, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer "as an act of loving devotion" uses the BSB's wording. The wrong answers are in plain modern wording, so the right answer stands out as the one that sounds like the Bible.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
